newsitem.title: UK: British charity denies kidnap report.
newsitem.headline: British charity denies kidnap report.

text.p: The British-based Save the Children Fund charity on Saturday denied a report that one of its aid workers had been kidnapped in Somalia.
"The report is inaccurate. No one has been kidnapped. All our staff are safe and well and we know where they are," spokeswoman Jenny Meadows told Reuters.

A group of the agency's workers had strayed into Ethiopia and were now "sorting out the bureaucratic misunderstanding" that resulted from having inadvertently crossed the border, Save the Children said.
Mark Bowden, the charity's regional director for East Africa, said the incident occurred on Friday in the border town of Feerfeer.
A group of seven Save the Childen workers were involved -- an Irish woman, a British man, four Somali men and a Somali man who holds and Ethiopian passport.
"We think they are quite safe in Ethiopia and expect to resolve the situation in the next couple of days," Bowden said.

Somali businessmen had earlier told Reuters in Mogadishu that an unnamed British woman working with the charity was taken away in Feerfeer by unidentified gunmen on Friday night. They said three of her Somali colleagues were also taken.
Lawless Somalia has been without a central administration since 1991 after rebels ousted late dictator Mohamed Siad Barre.
